brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.
requirements.evidence: Build has one drawer (drawer:0#0,1#cut, cell 0,1 cut face) and one spike (spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0) at junction of cells 0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0. Both sit at that shared corner of cell 0,1; check_build meshClash is clear.

requirements.requirement: The spike sits at that same corner of that same cell as the drawer, touching it.
requirements.evidence: The spike's junction (0,0|0,1|1,0) includes cell 0,1, where the drawer sits. The drawer was offered only on a half base's cut face, so the half-n base at 0,1 carries it; the spike is offered at the junction with that cell present.

finish.summary: Built a drawer and a spike at the same corner of cell (0,1). Cells (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0) meet at one junction; the spike sits there and the drawer sits in the cut face of the half-n base at (0,1). A drawer on (1,0) instead blocked the spike, so (0,1) was used. check_build: meshClash clear, no errors. Remaining warning is LOOSE_BODY on the two half bases, which the brief did not cover; joint bolts would lock them.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
